extracted.intended_audience: authors and contributors preparing Cochrane systematic reviews of interventions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and maintaining Cochrane systematic reviews of healthcare interventions, covering standard methods (planning, searching, bias assessment, analysis, GRADE) and specialised topics. Intended as the official reference that all Cochrane review authors should consult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Cochrane Handbook as the official guide
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions is the official guide that describes in detail the process of preparing and maintaining Cochrane systematic reviews on the effects of healthcare interventions. All authors should consult the Handbook for guidance on the methods used in Cochrane systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors of Cochrane reviews are expected to follow the Handbook's guidance when preparing reviews; it covers standard methods and specialised topics and links to Methodological Expectations (MECIR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning a review
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on planning a review (listed as a standard method applicable to every review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning is presented as a core methodological area in the Handbook; authors should consult the relevant chapter(s) for detailed expectations on scope, objectives, protocols, and review planning steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching and selecting studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on searching for studies and selecting eligible studies (listed as a standard method applicable to every review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook provides methods for designing search strategies, database selection, grey literature searching, and transparent inclusion/exclusion processes; consult chapter details for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on data collection for systematic reviews (listed as a standard method applicable to every review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes approaches to data extraction, data management, handling missing data, and procedures to ensure accuracy and reproducibility; see relevant Handbook chapters for templates and recommended processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on assessing risk of bias in included studies (listed as a standard method applicable to every review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook details recommended tools and procedures for assessing study-level bias, how to judge domains of bias, and how to incorporate risk-of-bias assessments into synthesis and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on statistical analysis for reviews (listed as a standard method applicable to every review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers meta-analysis methods, choice of effect measures, heterogeneity assessment, model selection, and sensitivity/subgroup analyses; refer to the statistical methods chapters for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE (grading quality of evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on using GRADE to assess the certainty/quality of the body of evidence (listed as a standard method applicable to every review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handbook includes instruction on applying GRADE domains (risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, publication bias) and producing summary of findings tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting results
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on interpreting review results (listed as a standard method applicable to every review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses translating quantitative/qualitative findings into conclusions, considering certainty of evidence, clinical importance, and implications for practice and future research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-randomized studies (specialised guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised Handbook guidance on reviews that include non-randomized studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains methodological considerations specific to non-randomized evidence, including bias sources, design-specific appraisal, and synthesis approaches; consult the relevant chapter when such studies are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse effects (specialised guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised Handbook guidance on identifying and analysing adverse effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides methods for searching, extracting, and synthesising harms data, including considerations of rare events and reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex interventions (specialised guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised Handbook guidance on reviews of complex interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers conceptualising complexity, multiple components/interactions, appropriate synthesis methods, and considerations for applicability and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity (specialised guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised Handbook guidance on equity considerations in systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers methods to identify and analyse differential effects across populations and to incorporate equity-focused questions into review design and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics (specialised guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised Handbook guidance on economic evidence and analyses in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses inclusion and appraisal of cost-effectiveness and economic evaluations, methods for synthesis of economic data, and reporting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient-reported outcomes (specialised guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised Handbook guidance on patient-reported outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes approaches to selecting, extracting, and synthesising PROMs (patient-reported outcome measures), handling multiple instruments, and interpreting clinical relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual patient data (IPD) reviews (specialised guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised Handbook guidance for reviews using individual patient data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers obtaining IPD, data management, analysis methods specific to IPD meta-analysis, and issues of data sharing and harmonisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective meta-analysis (specialised guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised Handbook guidance on prospective meta-analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes planning and coordinating prospective meta-analyses, registration, protocol harmonisation, and pre-specified analysis approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative research (specialised guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised Handbook guidance on incorporating qualitative research in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides methods for searching for, appraising, and synthesising qualitative evidence and integrating qualitative and quantitative findings where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological Expectations for Cochrane Intervention Reviews (MECIR) core standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Key aspects of Handbook guidance are collated as the Methodological Expectations for Cochrane Intervention Reviews (MECIR). These provide core standards that are generally expected of Cochrane reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each MECIR item includes a link to a relevant Handbook chapter; MECIR represents the set of procedural and methodological standards Cochrane reviews are generally expected to meet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing the Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions on how to cite the full Handbook online and the print edition, and that details for citing individual chapters are available in each chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides specific citation formats (example: Higgins JPT, Thomas J, Chandler J, Cumpston M, Li T, Page MJ, et al, editor(s). Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5 (updated August 2024). Cochrane, 2024. Available from www.cochrane.org/handbook). Ensure correct citation style and version when referencing the Handbook or individual chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to re-use Handbook material
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for academic/non-commercial and commercial reuse of Handbook material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short quotations may be used without requesting permission but must be appropriately cited. Reproducing material (screenshots, exact figures or tables, lengthy direct quotations of more than 5 lines) requires filling a permission request form to be approved by the Handbook editors; if approved, reuse is free with acknowledgement. Commercial reuse requires contacting Wiley Global Permissions (John Wiley & Sons, Ltd).

rubrics_metrics.name: Versioning and archived copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on previous versions of the Handbook and where to find details on changes between versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the 'Versions and changes' page for details on how the Handbook has changed and may access archived copies of prior versions (lists versions and dates). Use the appropriate version when citing or following procedures.
